headline: Subscriber growth and ad rebound drive sharp profit gains
summary_short: Revenue rose 12.0% y/y to $712.2M as digital-only subscribers grew to 13.08 million (+310,000 q/q, +1.46 million y/y) and digital advertising jumped 31.6%; diluted EPS was $0.54 versus $0.30 a year ago on a 54.5% rise in operating profit to $90.6M.
summary_long: Revenue grew 12.0% y/y, led by subscription revenue (+11.3%) as digital-only subscribers reached 13.08 million and digital ARPU rose 2.4% to $9.77 on subscribers moving off promotional pricing. Advertising revenue rose 17.3% on a 31.6% jump in digital advertising, partly offset by a 9.8% print decline. Operating profit rose 54.5% to $90.6M as revenue growth outpaced a 7.7% rise in operating costs, mainly higher journalism compensation and marketing spend. A lower effective tax rate (10.6% vs 22.5%) further lifted net income to $87.9M; diluted EPS was $0.54 versus $0.30. Cash plus marketable securities totaled $1.1B; free cash flow fell to $81.5M from $89.9M. The quarterly dividend was raised to $0.23/share. No numeric forward guidance was disclosed.

drivers.explanation: Digital subscriber growth, higher ARPU from promotional-to-standard price transitions, and a rebound in digital advertising drove double-digit revenue growth and a sharp rise in operating profit and EPS.

Growth came from an 11.3% rise in subscription revenue (digital-only +16.1% on +1.46M net subscriber adds y/y and +2.4% ARPU) and a 17.3% rise in advertising revenue, led by a 31.6% jump in digital advertising.

Gross profit (revenue less cost of revenue) rose as 12.0% revenue growth outpaced an 8.5% increase in cost of revenue, driven mainly by higher journalism compensation and cloud-related content-delivery costs.

Operating profit rose 54.5% as revenue growth outpaced a 7.7% rise in operating costs, led by higher journalism and sales compensation and marketing spend, partly offset by lower severance expense.
Pretax income rose in step with operating profit; interest income and other, net increased to $11.3M from $10.0M, while non-operating pension costs were roughly flat.
Net income rose with operating profit and was further lifted by a lower effective tax rate (10.6% vs 22.5%), reflecting a higher tax benefit from stock-based awards that settled in the quarter.
EPS rose with net income; average basic shares outstanding fell slightly y/y (162.0M vs 163.8M) on ongoing buybacks, modestly amplifying the per-share gain.
Diluted EPS tracked net income growth; diluted share count was down slightly y/y (163.7M vs 164.9M) on share repurchases outpacing equity-award dilution.

Operating cash flow fell y/y primarily because the prior-year quarter included nonrecurring proceeds from a land sale and this year saw higher incentive-compensation payments, partly offset by higher net income.

Cash fell q/q mainly due to $56.3M of share repurchases, $52.4M of stock-award tax withholding, and $30.4M of dividend payments, partly offset by operating cash inflow and marketable-securities maturities.
Equity fell q/q as dividends ($37.8M), share repurchases ($56.3M) and net stock-award withholding taxes (~$52.4M combined) exceeded net income ($87.9M) and stock-based compensation ($19.3M).
Diluted share count fell slightly y/y as ongoing repurchases ($56.3M this quarter, fully using the 2023 authorization) outpaced new issuance from equity awards.
